findings_qualitative.value: No 12CO outflow wings detected toward the Papillon YSO.

evidence.quote: neither the Papillon Nebula YSO nor J054009.49-694453.5 have $^{12}$CO(2-1) outflow wing detections

claims.hypothesis: Was the Papillon YSO formation triggered by filament collision?
claims.experiment: PV diagrams and velocity components of three filaments
claims.result: Three velocity filaments merge at the YSO; broadened lines span ~9 km/s
claims.finding: Collision of filaments likely triggered the O star formation

evidence.quote: It is natural that a similar filamentary collision, possibly a triple collision, took place in Papillon.

claims.hypothesis: Is the Papillon YSO beginning to disperse its cloud?
claims.experiment: CO, H30alpha, continuum and temperature slices
claims.result: 0.6 pc CO hole filled by ionized gas, ~80 K gas at its edge
claims.finding: The YSO has begun dispersing its parent cloud

evidence.quote: The distribution of molecular gas toward the Papillon Nebula shows a CO-hole with a diameter of $\sim 0.6$ pc.

limitations_admitted.value: 12CO-based mass may be inaccurate in optically thick or heated gas.

evidence.quote: The mass estimation from the $^{12}$CO intensity may be inaccurate in the optically thick region of the high column density

referee_caveats_inferred: Collision claim rests on two-point velocity coincidences and projected geometry

Only two high-mass YSOs support the generalization
